title: introduce-client-capability-headers-and-schema-telemetry-compat-layer
author: Sofia Chen
release_notes: Add optional client capability headers for schema negotiation; add telemetry for schema-version usage and enable a transparent compat layer that maps legacy tool envelopes to the new structured output format. No forced behavior changes for existing clients unless they opt in via beta header.
description:
Context and motivation: We need a safe, observable path to evolve request/response schemas without breaking streaming or tool-calling integrations. Over the last quarter customers and internal telemetry show a mix of v1 and v2 schema usage; when we rolled structured output changes into beta some clients experienced silent truncation in streaming tool responses. This PR introduces a small, opt-in client capability handshake and server-side compatibility layer so we can: 1) detect client capabilities at request time, 2) emit telemetry for schema versions and fallback events, and 3) apply server-side translation shims to preserve behavior for legacy clients while allowing newer clients to opt into the stricter v2 structured responses.

What this PR does (high level): Adds three optional headers, a lightweight negotiator middleware, and a rewriter/adapter pipeline: - New headers: X-Client-Schema-Capabilities (comma-separated tokens), X-Schema-Beta-Opt-In (boolean), X-Schema-Deprecated-At (RFC3339 timestamp) for server-issued deprecation signals. - Schema negotiator middleware (web/api/handlers/schema_negotiator.py): reads headers, augments request context with client_capabilities, and routes through the compatibility pipeline when needed. - Compat adapters (runtime/compat/legacy_tool_adapter.rs): maps legacy tool/function-call envelopes to the v2 structured output envelope used by the runtime, preserving call semantics and KV cache markers for streaming. - Streaming framer improvements (runtime/streaming/stream_framer.cu): introduce explicit chunk boundary markers for tool-call frames to avoid ambiguous boundaries during chunked transport. - Telemetry pipeline additions (observability/telemetry/schema_usage_pipeline.yml + SDK hooks): record per-request schema preference, negotiated fallback reason, and whether translation was applied. - Docs and SDK: documentation explaining headers and migration steps (docs/api/versioning.md) plus a small client helper in Python (sdk/python/redwood/schema_capability.py).

Backward compatibility guarantees: - No client-observable behavioral changes unless the client sets X-Schema-Beta-Opt-In=true or advertises a capability that requires v2. - For legacy clients, the compat adapter rewrites server responses to the legacy envelope format. For streaming tool calls, chunk markers ensure correct reassembly. - Deprecation flow: servers may start including X-Schema-Deprecated-At to indicate planned sunset of a legacy envelope; SDK helpers will surface warnings when present.

Implementation notes and design tradeoffs: - We opted for headers over request-body flags to keep early routing decisions cheap and to work with existing proxies/load-balancers. - The compat layer is pluggable and lives in runtime/compat so it can be toggled per-deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private). - Telemetry uses a dedicated small event schema to avoid inflating per-token metrics; we intentionally record negotiation events rather than full payloads.

Checklist: - [x] Negotiator middleware implemented and unit tested - [x] Compat adapter implements main legacy->v2 path and translation tests - [x] Streaming framer updated with chunk markers and e2e test covering tool call boundaries - [x] SDK helper for Python added and documented - [x] Docs guide + migration steps added to docs/api/versioning.md - [x] Telemetry pipeline config committed - [x] Integration/e2e tests updated - [x] Backwards-compat assertions in CI (legacy clients still pass)

Commits (summary): - 1a4b2c: add negotiator middleware and header parsing - 2b6d9f: implement legacy_tool_adapter core translations - 3c7e51: streaming framer chunk boundary support + tests - 4f0aee: telemetry events and pipeline config - 5b2caa: docs and SDK helper - 6e99f1: fix race in streaming framer under high-concurrency (addressed reviewer feedback)

Files/areas touched (high level): - web/api/handlers: negotiation and routing hooks - runtime/compat: adapters and translation logic - runtime/streaming: framer changes that add explicit markers and assert boundaries - sdk/python: helper class and convenience function to advertise capabilities - docs: migration and header reference - observability: pipeline and dashboards for schema usage

Testing and CI: Initial CI run flagged a flaky e2e around stream reassembly (test_schema_negotiation.py). I reproduced locally under heavy concurrency and fixed a race by turning one atomic counter into an epoch-ordered sequence marker (6e99f1). After the fix all checks passed (unit/integration/e2e + lint + mypy). CI summary: 12/12 jobs passed on final run.

Review conversation (high level): - Asha Kapoor (review): asked for clearer guarantees around reserialized timestamps and KV cache equality; author added deterministic timestamp roundtrip tests and a comment block documenting invariants. - Miguel Alvarez (review): requested telemetry rate-limiting to avoid event storms; author added a sampling knob and conservative default (0.1%) and noted this can be configured per-customer. - Liam O'Connor (approver): suggested adding a short migration note to the change log which was added. There was a small thread where security flagged header naming; we landed on X-Schema-* to avoid collision.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind a feature flag (runtime.compat.enabled=false by default). 2) Enable telemetry in staging, monitor schema_negotiation.count and fallback.rate dashboards. 3) Open an early access program inviting a handful of customers to opt into X-Schema-Beta-Opt-In=true; gather feedback on structured outputs for tool-call workflows. 4) Gradually enable runtime.compat.enabled=true for internal traffic, then fully for hosted after two weeks of stable telemetry.

Why this is different from previous schema shims: Prior PRs implemented coarse-grained fallback or global rewrites. This change introduces an explicit client-declared capability handshake and per-request telemetry that lets us quantitatively measure migration and fallback without risking silent regressions in streaming tool boundaries. The chunk marker approach reduces a whole class of nondeterministic reassembly bugs in the presence of transport chunking and proxies.

Known limitations and follow-ups: - This PR does not implement server-side automatic schema coercion for ambiguous structured fields (follow-up ENG-9041). - Private installer playbooks will need an opt-in flag change; the private-installer team has a linked Linear ticket. - We rely on header propagation through proxies; customers on extremely locked-down networks may require explicit proxy rules.

If merged: update changelog, enable feature-flag in staging, and notify SRE + Docs to prepare the migration guide in the customer portal.
short_summary: Adds optional client capability headers, server negotiator middleware, a compat adapter for legacy tool envelopes, streaming framer boundary markers, and telemetry to observe schema negotiation and fallback events. Opt-in beta flow; no forced breaking changes.
notes_for_release: Opt-in headers: X-Client-Schema-Capabilities, X-Schema-Beta-Opt-In, server may emit X-Schema-Deprecated-At. Backwards-compatible by default. SDK helper and docs included.
final_ci_log: All jobs passed after rerun: unit-tests, integration-tests, e2e (flaky fixed), lint, mypy. 12/12 jobs green.
